record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: Fix integers t and n with 4 ≤ t ≤ n. Let g_{K_t}(n) be the maximum size of a family of graphs on vertex set [n] such that the intersection of any two graphs in the family contains a copy of K_t. Is g_{K_t}(n) exactly 2^{(n choose 2) - (t choose 2)}? Equivalently, is the largest possible K_t-intersecting family always obtained by fixing one copy of K_t and taking all graphs that contain it?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1. For all t, n ∈ N with 4 ≤ t ≤ n, gKt(n) = 2^((n choose 2)−(t choose 2)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $t$ and $n$ with $4 \le t \le n$, consider graphs on the labeled vertex set $[n] = \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$; each such graph is identified with its edge set, a subset of $\binom{[n]}{2}$. Say that a family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs on $[n]$ is $K_t$-intersecting if for every pair $G_1, G_2 \in \mathcal{F}$, the intersection $G_1 \cap G_2$ (the graph on $[n]$ whose edge set is the intersection of the edge sets of $G_1$ and $G_2$) contains a copy of the complete graph $K_t$ as a subgraph. Let $g_{K_t}(n)$ denote the maximum possible size of a $K_t$-intersecting family of graphs on $[n]$. One construction is to fix a copy of $K_t$ in $[n]$ and take all graphs on $[n]$ containing it, giving a $K_t$-intersecting family of size $2^{\binom{n}{2} - \binom{t}{2}}$.

Prove or disprove: for all integers $t, n$ with $4 \le t \le n$,
$$g_{K_t}(n) = 2^{\binom{n}{2} - \binom{t}{2}}.$$
Equivalently, is the largest $K_t$-intersecting family of graphs on $[n]$ always obtained (up to isomorphism) by fixing a copy of $K_t$ and taking all graphs containing it?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is known for t=3 (triangle-intersecting families, proved by Ellis, Filmus, and Friedgut) and for t=4 (K_4-intersecting families, established in arXiv:2103.12671, which also gives a corresponding product/cross-intersecting bound and stability result). For general t ≥ 5, the conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: K4-INTERSECTING FAMILIES OF GRAPHS
status_evidence.snippet: if two families F₁ and F₂ of graphs on n vertices are such that for any G₁ ∈ F₁ and G₂ ∈ F₂, G₁ ∩ G₂ contains a K₄, then |F₁||F₂| ≤ 4^(C(n,2) - C(4,2)), with equality only when both families consist of all graphs containing a fixed K₄. ... proving the result for both triangle-intersecting (t=3) and K₄-intersecting (t=4) families.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proved for t=3 and t=4, leaving t ≥ 5 open.
